title: Protocol for evaluating protein relocalization from the plasma membrane to chloroplasts
protocol: Culture A. tumefaciens strain GV3101 harboring corresponding binary vectors in 10 mL liquid LB with appropriate antibiotics at 28°C and shaking at 180 rpm overnight.
Harvest the bacteria by centrifugation at 4,000 × g for 10 minutes.
Resuspend the harvested bacteria in infiltration buffer (10 mM MgCl2, 10 mM MES pH 5.6, 150 mM acetosyringone) to an OD600 of 0.2-0.6.
Incubate bacterial suspensions at room temperature (23°C–25°C) in the dark for 2 hours.
Infiltrate abaxial side of leaves of four-week-old N. benthamiana plants with a 1 mL needle-less syringe using resuspended bacteria.
Use the third and fourth youngest fully expanded leaves for infiltration, infiltrating two leaves per plant to achieve desired protein levels.
Infiltrate the abaxial side of selected leaves from a four-week-old N. benthamiana plant with an agroinfiltration mixture using a needle-less syringe.
Mix A. tumefaciens suspensions carrying different constructs at a 1:1 ratio before infiltration for co-infiltration experiments.
Infiltrate the bacterial suspension until the whole leaf area appears translucent.
Ensure that infiltrated leaves do not touch each other after infiltration.
Gently dry excess bacterial suspension with a paper towel.
Cut small leaf discs from plants expressing C4-GFP and C4G2A-GFP two days after Agrobacterium tumefaciens infiltration.
Place the leaf discs on a microscope slide.
Put a drop of water on the microscope slide with the leaf disc.
Cover the leaf disc and water with a coverslip.
Observe under a confocal microscope using a GFP filter with excitation/emission: 488/500–550 nm.
Infiltrate N. benthamiana leaves expressing the viral protein C4-GFP with CHX (180 μM) two days after Agrobacterium infiltration and verification of protein accumulation.
Incubate infiltrated leaves for 2 hours.
Infiltrate one-half of the leaf with PAMP flg22 (1 μM).
Infiltrate the other half of the leaf with water as mock treatment.
Harvest 6 leaves (2 leaves from each plant) after 6–8 h for protein and chloroplast isolations using fresh tissue.
Harvest leaf samples after 12–24 h for visualization under the confocal microscope.
Cut small leaf discs from plants expressing C4-GFP and C4G2A-GFP after 16 h of flg22 or mock treatment using a corkborer with plunger (4 mm diameter).
Place the leaf discs on a microscope slide.
Put a drop of water over the leaf discs.
Cover the leaf discs with a coverslip.
Observe under a confocal microscope using GFP filter with excitation/emission: 488/500–550 nm.
Visualize chloroplasts using chlorophyll autofluorescence at excitation/emission: 488/650–700 nm.
Calculate the final relative quantification values as the ratio of PM to chloroplast fluorescence intensity.
Use fresh tissue for isolation of intact chloroplasts.
Check the expression of the GFP-tagged protein by confocal microscopy prior to chloroplast isolation.
Carry out the chloroplast isolation in low or dim light (20 μmol m−2 s−1).
Perform the experiment in a cold room if possible; otherwise, keep all materials at 4°C.
Collect plant leaf materials into a beaker placed on ice.
Use wide-bore 1 mL tips for the isolation of chloroplasts.
Cut 2 mm off the tip of 1 mL pipetman tips using a razor blade.
Autoclave and dry the modified tips.
Grind the tissue (around 6 leaves of four-weeks-old N. benthamiana plants) in 50 mL of isolation buffer using a Waring blender, repeating three times for 3 seconds each.
Filter the homogenate through 4 layers of Miracloth into a 50 mL polypropylene tube.
Centrifuge the filtered homogenate at 400 × g for 8 minutes.
Collect and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL of isolation buffer.
Suspend the pellet from each tube in approximately 250 μL of isolation buffer if using multiple tubes, then pool all suspensions together.
Load 500–1000 μL of chloroplast suspension onto a two-step Percoll gradient.
Centrifuge the loaded chloroplast suspension at 200 × g for 20 minutes in a swing-out rotor with brakes off.
Remove broken chloroplasts and Percoll until reaching the layer of intact chloroplasts between the two Percoll steps.
Take the intact chloroplasts using a wide-bore tip, place into a 50 mL tube, fill with HS buffer up to 50 mL, invert the tube several times, and centrifuge at 400 × g for 6 minutes.
Resuspend the chloroplast pellet in another 50 mL of HS buffer and centrifuge at 400 × g for 6 minutes.
Resuspend the final chloroplast pellet in 1 mL of HS buffer.
Take a 10 μL aliquot.
Add 990 μL of 80% acetone to the aliquot.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Centrifuge for 5 minutes at 21,000 × g at room temperature (23°C–25°C).
Take the clear supernatant.
Measure OD652 using a quartz or glass cuvette.
Calculate chlorophyll concentration as Chl (mg/mL) = (OD652 × dilution factor)/36.
Take a volume of intact chloroplasts suspension corresponding to a desired amount of chlorophyll.
Pellet down the suspension at 2600 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in 150 μL of HM buffer and keep on ice for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the resuspended pellet at 2600 × g for 5 minutes.
Separate the supernatant as stroma fraction (150 μL).
Separate the pellet as membrane (envelopes and thylakoids) fraction.
Remove contaminants by washing the membrane fraction with HS buffer.
Collect 2 leaf discs with an 8-mm punch from each leaf.
Grind the collected leaf discs in liquid nitrogen and transfer to 2 mL tubes.
Store the tubes at −80°C until chloroplast isolation.
Isolate intact chloroplasts from the leaves used for leaf disc collection.
Resuspend the isolated chloroplast pellet corresponding to 1000 μg of chlorophyll in 1 mL protein extraction buffer.
Resuspend the leaf disc powder collected earlier in 500 μL protein extraction buffer.
Incubate resuspended samples on a revolver lab rotator at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge samples at 21,000 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Collect supernatant from the centrifuged sample and repeat centrifugation if necessary.
Final supernatants represent chloroplast proteins (from isolated chloroplasts) and total leaf proteins (from ground leaf discs).
Take 150 μL of each protein sample.
Add 50 μL of 4× Laemmli sample buffer to the protein samples.
Denature the mixed samples at 95°C for 10 minutes.
Load equal amounts of denatured chloroplast and total proteins on 10% SDS-PAGE gels.
Transfer gel contents to PVDF membranes via wet or semi-dry transfer methods.
Mix 15 mM sterile HCl with human recombinant leptin.
Prepare fresh working solutions for injection 30 minutes before each injection time point.
Visualize the target protein using a specific antibody.
Use light-harvesting complex proteins (LhcBs) as membrane marker proteins for detection.
Use Rubisco large subunit proteins (RbcL) as stroma marker proteins for detection.
Stain the gel with CBB to confirm equal loading of samples.
Stain the membrane with Ponceau S staining to confirm equal protein loading.
Quantify proteins bands in western blots using ImageJ.
Make a copy of original raw images from western blots.
Save copied images as JPEG file format.
Transform the image mode to “Grayscale”.
Click on the “Analyze” menu and select “Set Measurements” in ImageJ software.
Keep only the “Mean gray value” checked in the checkboxes.
Open the JPEG file images generated previously using the “File” menu.
Set a defined “Region of Interest” (ROI) size according to the largest band among the target bands of a sample on the blot.
Click on the “Analyze” menu and then on “Tools”.
In the “ROI Manager menu”, set a defined ROI size.
Select the “rectangle” tool and draw a frame around the largest band.
Adjust the size of the frame so that it covers the minimum area.
Click the “File” menu, select “Save as”, choose “Selection”, and save this frame.
Use the same frame for all the protein bands you need to analyze from the same blot.
If accidentally resized or lost, go to the “File” menu, click “Open”, and reimport the same frame again.
Put the frame so that the band is inside, click the “Analyze” menu, select “Measure”, and get the intensity values.
Move the frame to the following bands and repeat this step in order to get the intensity values for all the samples.
Export the values into a spreadsheet keeping track of which value corresponds to which sample.
Repeat the steps to take a background measurement using the same frame as for the protein bands.
Put the frame above or below every band on the row where there are no other bands, get the intensity values, and export into the spreadsheet.
For the loading control bands, repeat the same steps as described for the sample bands.
With all the values in the spreadsheet, proceed to do the calculations.
Apply the formula 255 – X, where X is the intensity value recorded for each band or loading control and their respective background values, to invert the pixel density for all data.
Calculate the net value for the protein bands by deducting the inverted background value from the inverted band value.
Calculate the relative value as the ratio of a net band value over the corresponding net loading control.
Save high-resolution images or scans from the blots or films in TIFF file format at 600 dpi.
Quantify isolated proteins using standard protocols, such as the PierceTM BCA protein assay kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific).
Take 150 μL of isolated chloroplast protein samples.
Add 50 μL of 4× Laemmli sample buffer to the protein samples.
Denature the mixture at 95°C for 10 minutes.
Incubate the desired amount of protein with 25 μL of antibody-conjugated beads (e.g., GFP-Trap Agarose beads) at 4°C for 1.5–2 hours while agitating.
Centrifuge the samples at 2500 × g for 30 seconds.
Wash the beads four times with wash buffer (PBS with 0.05% Triton X-100) for 5 minutes each.
Elute bound proteins in 100 μL of 1× Laemmli SDS sample buffer by incubating at 70°C for 20 minutes.
Load equal amounts of input and IP-eluted samples on a 10% SDS-PAGE gel (load 10 μL for bait protein, load varies for prey protein).
Transfer the gel to PVDF membranes via wet or semi-dry transfer methods.
Visualize the protein of interest using a specific antibody or tag-specific antibody.
Stain the gel with CBB and the membrane with Ponceau S to show equal loading.
